thread:
maria (support): hi team — customer A reported SSO logins started failing after they pushed a metadata change this morning. All users see an error: 'SAML response signature invalid'. ticket #12345. @john can you take a look?

john (eng): on it. do we have their metadata URL and a sample error stack?

maria (support): metadata: https://idp.customer-a.com/saml/metadata.xml — error from our logs: `SignatureException: signature verification failed (fingerprint mismatch)`

ingrid (sre): quick sanity check — I fetched metadata with curl, got a 301 to CDN + gzip. headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
Location: https://cdn.customer-a.com/metadata/abcd
Content-Encoding: gzip
Vary: Accept-Encoding
```

saml-validator-bot: automated run against metadata URL returned: `XMLParseError: invalid token at start of document` when fed raw bytes (no decompression). When decompressed, validator finds two KeyDescriptor entries; one with old cert (SHA1 fingerprint) and one with new cert (SHA256).

john (eng): aha. I think our metadata fetcher did a plain GET and fed the body to the XML parser without handling `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Some HTTP clients automatically decompress, some don't — if we parsed compressed bytes as-is, the XML parser would choke and our fallback fingerprint logic could pick the wrong cert.

maria (support): customer says they didn't change cert rotation order intentionally, just re-uploaded metadata via their CI. They claim curl --compressed shows a valid XML with new cert.

ingrid (sre): repro steps I ran:
1) `curl -sI https://idp.customer-a.com/saml/metadata.xml` -> 301 -> CDN
2) `curl -s https://cdn.customer-a.com/metadata/abcd -o meta.gz` (saved bytes)
3) `file meta.gz` -> "gzip compressed data"
4) `gunzip -c meta.gz | xmllint --noout -` -> valid XML, new cert first, old cert second
But if you do `curl -s https://cdn.customer-a.com/metadata/abcd | xmllint --noout -` it fails because curl didn't decompress by default on that host.

john (eng): good find. our fetcher library (internal http-client v2) sets `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` normally, but a recent change to enable streaming fetches bypassed the auto-decompress. Streaming fetch returned raw gz bytes to the SAML parser. That explains intermittent failures (some fetchers decompress, others don't).

maria (support): customer reported 100% failures after they updated their CDN config to add `Vary: Accept-Encoding` — matches the timing.

john (eng): proposed fix: update our metadata fetch path to explicitly request `Accept-Encoding: identity` so we always get uncompressed XML, or ensure streaming path performs Content-Encoding handling. I'll open a patch.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch `http-client` -> ensure `Content-Encoding` handled in streaming paths (PR #4821).

john (eng): patch pushed to staging. test plan: pull metadata URL via our fetcher, validate we get decompressed XML, run saml-validator -> should parse, compute fingerprint for new cert. Also add unit test simulating gzipped response.

ingrid (sre): i'm going to rerun customer login against staging endpoint now.

saml-validator-bot: staging run: metadata parsed, cert fingerprints: [`sha256:AA:BB:CC:...`], validation OK.

ingrid (sre): verified end-to-end on staging with customer's metadata URL. SSO flow succeeds for test user.

maria (support): relayed to customer, they confirmed logins are working now. They changed their CDN compression config back as a workaround.

john (eng): closing root cause — streaming fetch path didn't honor Content-Encoding, leading to parser errors and fallback behavior that computed wrong fingerprint. Fix: handle Content-Encoding in streaming path + unit tests + add a transient metric for metadata fetch decompression failures.

maria (support): great. i'll mark ticket #12345 resolved and include notes: "cause: gzipped metadata returned by CDN; our metadata fetcher didn't decompress streaming response; fixed in http-client v2 patch." :white_check_mark:

ingrid (sre): FYI i'll add a short health check that fetches critical customers' metadata with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` and `identity` to detect CDN oddities early. :eyes:

john (eng): reassigning follow-up tasks: (1) backport to 1.x branch, (2) add observability alert for `metadata_parse_errors` spike, (3) ship grace-period retry that fetches with `Accept-Encoding: identity` on parse failure.

maria (support): thanks team. closing thread.
